name: Miach

attributes.attribute: an Irish god of healing, son of Dian Cécht
made skin grow around Nuada's silver hand and restored him

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Miach was an Irish god of healing. He was the son of the physician god Dian Cécht and the brother of the herbalist Airmid. Miach himself was a brilliant doctor and magician. King Nuada lost his hand in the second battle of Mag Tuired and lost his throne because of the blemish. Dian Cécht made a hand of silver that worked like a real hand, but the silver hand did not end the taboo against a blemished king. Only Miach's magic healed Nuada and restored him to the throne. Dian Cécht could not accept his son's success. Out of envy he killed Miach. The most powerful herbs in the world grew on Miach's grave. Airmid tended them until they were ready to harvest, then sorted them by the good they brought. Dian Cécht again interfered and scrambled the categories, so the healing knowledge was lost to humankind. The name Miach may come from the Middle Irish word midach, meaning doctor.
